name: Ganga (Ganges)
fact: The Ganga is one of the longest rivers in India and is sacred to many people. It begins in the Himalayas and flows toward the Bay of Bengal.

name: Yamuna
fact: The Yamuna joins the Ganga at Prayagraj. Many cities along it work to keep the water clean.

name: Brahmaputra
fact: The Brahmaputra flows through Assam and carries lots of water during the monsoon. Its valley is famous for tea.

name: Godavari
fact: Sometimes called the ‘Dakshina Ganga’, the Godavari is the longest river in peninsular India.

name: Krishna
fact: The Krishna River helps farmers in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.

name: Narmada
fact: The Narmada flows west to the Arabian Sea between tall cliffs that geologists love to study.

name: Kaveri (Cauvery)
fact: The Kaveri supports farming in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and is important for irrigation.

name: Mahanadi
fact: The Mahanadi runs through Chhattisgarh and Odisha and feeds many irrigation projects.

name: Indus
fact: The ancient Indus Valley Civilisation gets its name from this river system.

name: Tapti (Tapi)
fact: The Tapti flows through central India and meets the Arabian Sea south of the Narmada.

name: Sabarmati
fact: The Sabarmati runs through Gujarat; Mahatma Gandhi’s ashram sat along its banks in Ahmedabad.

name: Teesta
fact: The Teesta rushes down from the Himalayas into the plains of West Bengal.
